text:
incident-bot: [P1] GPU OOM during prefill detected on us-west-2-node-17. Container restarted x3. Trigger: prefill_memory > 40GB. Auto-evict attempted. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-prefill-oom

jess-oncall: oncall here, acknowledging. Paging SREs, putting a 15m watch. Any immediate customer impact?

mike-sre: looking at logs now. seeing repeated CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS followed by oom-kill in runtime container. Prefill KV cache grew to ~48GB for a single request (long-context, ~1.2M tokens payload) and triggered container OOM.

carla-ml: which model? saw this with redwood-xt-30b-64k (quantized). Long single-user history + streaming prefill caused unbounded kvcache growth.

infra-bot: auto-evict kicked in and moved 2 pods off node-17; node flapped once (kubelet restarted). No node-level hardware failure reported.

jess-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) disable long-context route on hosted-prod, 2) enable per-request kvcache cap + backpressure, 3) route heavy requests to dedicated capacity fallback. Applying 1 now.

jess-oncall: applying patch to runtime:
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch deployment/runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/disable-long-context":"true"}}}}}'
```

deploy-bot: patch applied to deployment/runtime-prod (rolling restart started). 3/10 pods restarted, 1 failed healthcheck and was recreated.

mike-sre: enabling on-the-fly kvcache eviction (kv_eviction_policy=aggressive) on the affected nodes. Observed memory drop from ~45GB -> ~18GB on node-17 within 40s. No further immediate restarts.

support-anna: Customer impact: noticed ~14 5xx errors between 12:32-12:36 UTC on long-context generate. Affected customers flagged: AcmeCorp (high-traffic), BetaApps (sampled errors). Drafting interim message.

support-anna: Draft to customers: "We detected elevated errors on long-context generation. We applied temporary mitigations and are monitoring. If you saw 5xx responses between 12:30-12:40 UTC, please share request IDs. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

carla-ml: follow-ups to prevent recurrence: add hard cap on kvcache entries per request, instrument "prefill_kv_entries" metric, and add circuit-breaker that returns 413/limit-exceeded for >200k token prefill. Also add config to penalize single-request kv growth in routing decisions.

mike-sre: agree. I'll open infra ticket to add per-request kv limits and a heuristic to detect streamed prefill abuse. Also recommend lowering default max_window for hosted API until we ship more robust memory accounting.

jess-oncall: handing off 30m watch to @ellie-night. If errors reappear or node flaps again, escalate to eng-runtime. Anna to send customer interim note once approved.

ellie-night: Ack — I'll monitor dashboards and logs for the next 30m. Leaving channel open.

mike-sre: recording timeline + root-candidate: unbounded kvcache growth on long streaming prefill => container OOM => kubelet restart => brief node flap. Will include kernel/CUDA traces in follow-up.

jess-oncall: good work team. Postmortem owners: eng-runtime + eng-ml. Assigning follow-up items: KV cap (mike-sre), routing & circuit-breaker (carla-ml), support comms (support-anna).

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> transitioning to watch state. Link: /incidents/1799999988
